title: Cardiovascular Drift During Prolonged Exercise: New Perspectives
claims: Cardiovascular drift begins after about 10 minutes of prolonged moderate-intensity exercise (50-75% VO2max) in a neutral or warm environment.
Classic drift is characterised by a progressive fall in stroke volume and a parallel rise in heart rate, while cardiac output remains nearly constant.
In the reviewed control condition, stroke volume fell 13% and heart rate rose 11% between 15 and 55 minutes, with a final core temperature of 37.8 degrees Celsius.
Preventing the rise in heart rate with mild beta-1 adrenoceptor blockade eliminated the fall in stroke volume, despite unchanged cutaneous blood flow.
Dehydration of 4.9% of body mass during 120 minutes at 35 degrees Celsius reduced stroke volume by 28% and cardiac output by 18%, and raised core temperature from 38.0 to 39.3 degrees Celsius.

Cutaneous blood flow stabilised after 20-30 minutes and was not temporally linked to the fall in stroke volume; stroke volume was similar at 35 and 8 degrees Celsius despite a four-fold difference in cutaneous blood flow.
Core temperature and heart rate during drift were strongly correlated (r-squared = 0.95).
